what_its_for: Dalfampridine is used to help improve walking in adults with multiple sclerosis (MS). It works by helping nerve signals travel more effectively along damaged nerves, which can make your steps stronger and faster.
how_to_take: Swallow the tablet whole with or without food. Do NOT crush, chew, split, or break the tablet — this is very important for your safety. Take it at the same times every day, about 12 hours apart (for example, 8 AM and 8 PM). This helps keep a steady level of medicine in your body.
dosing: The usual dose is one 10 mg tablet twice a day, taken about 12 hours apart. Never take more than 2 tablets in one day. Taking too much greatly increases your risk of having a seizure.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, skip it and just take your next scheduled dose at the regular time. Never take 2 doses at the same time or within 12 hours of each other to make up for a missed dose.
storage: Store at room temperature between 59°F and 77°F (15°C to 25°C). Keep the tablets in their original container, away from moisture and heat. Keep out of reach of children.
what_to_avoid: Avoid taking more than the prescribed dose — extra doses can cause seizures. Avoid driving or operating heavy machinery until you know how this medicine affects you, as it can cause dizziness or balance problems. Let your doctor know about ALL other medications you take, including over-the-counter drugs and supplements, before starting this medicine.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or go to the emergency room if you have a seizure (shaking, loss of consciousness). Also contact your doctor if you experience: signs of a urinary tract infection (burning with urination, needing to go more often, fever), new or worsening back pain, weakness, numbness, tingling, trouble urinating, severe dizziness or loss of balance, or allergic reactions such as hives, swelling of your face, lips, or throat, or difficulty breathing.
when_it_works: Some people notice improvement in walking ability within a few weeks of starting the medication. However, not everyone responds to this medicine. If you do not notice any improvement in walking after a few weeks, talk to your doctor about whether to continue.
special_populations: This medicine is NOT recommended if you have kidney problems (even mild), because the drug can build up in your body and raise your risk of seizures. It is also NOT recommended if you have a history of seizures or epilepsy. If you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding, talk to your doctor before taking this medicine, as the effects on unborn babies or infants are not fully known. Older adults may need extra monitoring since kidney function often decreases with age.
